newsitem.title: USA: Washington State Gov vetoes property tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Washington State Gov vetoes property tax cut.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke has vetoed a measure that would have capped annual state and local property tax increases at the rate of inflation.
Instead Locke, a Democrat, proposed a tax credit that would return $217 million to homeowners over the next two years.

Locke, in announcing the veto late Wednesday before a midnight deadline, said the Legislature's plan to cap increases in property tax collections would have violated the state constitution by assessing properties differently.
And Locke said the measure would have done nothing to correct the imbalance in tax relief between businesses and homeowners.

Instead Locke proposed giving homeowners an exemption from state property taxes on the first $29,000 in assessed value. That would give each homeowner a $111 tax credit in 1998, rising to $138 in 2001.
"The people of the state deserve a comprehensive approach to property tax reform rather than the short-sighted, piecemeal approach taken by the Legislature so far," Locke said in his veto message.
But Locke's proposal would require an amendment to the state constitution, meaning a two-thirds vote in each house of the Republican-controlled Legislature, which political leaders said was unlikely.

Locke previously signed into law a 4.7 percent state property tax reduction that will mean about $17 to the owner of a typical $100,000 home. But he declined to approve a measure making that cut permanent.
Republicans have said they plan to roll the two tax cut measures into a single proposal and bring them directly to voters on the November ballot, which Locke could not veto.
